clue.text: Place for yachtsmen, rain-splashed in Massachusetts?

indicators.note: the shuffled word sits inside the state abbreviation, as the clue's 'in Massachusetts' says

parts.note: MA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Massachusetts

indicators.note: rain splashed about is scattered, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A harbour for sailors where the rain splashes down, somewhere on the Massachusetts coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splashed' rearranges RAIN to ARIN, and 'in' puts that inside MA.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbour with moorings for pleasure boats is a place yachtsmen keep their craft.

clue.text: Strange Celts' circle found in recess

indicators.note: strange suggests something odd or out of place, so the letters of Celts plus the ring are rearranged

parts.note: a circle is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: An odd Celtic stone circle is discovered tucked away in an alcove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' rearranges CELTS together with O (the circle) to give a word for a small room.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupboard or small private room is a recess set into a wall.

clue.text: Bad riot in unions, perhaps, leads to mutiny

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the words before it are only one possible arrangement, so their letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Unruly behaviour in trade unions escalates into outright rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges all fifteen letters of BAD RIOT IN UNIONS; 'leads to' joins wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Refusing to obey orders, especially aboard ship or in the army, is the essence of a mutiny.

clue.text: Priest has been in trouble outside with such a direct approach

indicators.note: outside tells us the shuffled word wraps around the priest's name
been in trouble is been in disorder, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: Eli is the priest of the Old Testament who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A clergyman who has got into difficulties heads straight for the problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' rearranges BEEN to BENE, and 'outside' wraps it around ELI.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase comes from the idea that a bee flies in a straight line home, so it means the most direct route.

clue.text: Like a Martini-Henry? Yes and no!

definitions.text: Like a Martini-Henry? Yes and no!

parts.words: Like a Martini-Henry? Yes and no!
parts.note: the Martini-Henry was a single-shot rifle, so it had one gun barrel, yet its hyphenated two-part name is the kind of surname described by the same term

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a Victorian rifle, answered with a playful contradiction.
explanation.walkthrough: The Martini-Henry was a British army rifle of the 1870s with a single barrel; the term also describes a hyphenated surname like its own, hence 'Yes and no'.
explanation.definitionFit: The term describes either a gun with two barrels or a hyphenated name, and the rifle fits only the second sense.

clue.text: Street ring ticks off dealer in commodities

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong or not right, so the letters of ticks are rearranged

explanation.surface: A street-corner trader has his stock checked off item by item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges TICKS to CKIST, which follows ST and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop or trader that keeps a particular product in stock for sale is a dealer in goods.

clue.text: Up-country centre

explanation.surface: Simply two words: an inland region and the middle of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Up-country is the inland part away from the coast, and a centre is the inner part of anything.

clue.text: Standard weapon speech

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level, as in 'up to par'
a lance is a long spear carried by a mounted knight

explanation.surface: A clipped phrase like a military report about a regulation-issue weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A way of speaking or a particular idiom is a form of speech.

clue.text: Trip over uranium ingot

indicators.note: over implies being knocked over and turned about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles over a bar of radioactive metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' rearranges U (uranium) with INGOT.
explanation.definitionFit: An excursion or day out is a short trip.

clue.text: Big Bird in The Muppets?

indicators.note: in signals that the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Asks whether the tall yellow bird from children's television belongs among Jim Henson's puppets.
explanation.walkthrough: Big Bird is the tall yellow puppet of Sesame Street, a Muppet; here it is just a large flightless bird hidden in thE MUppets.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian flightless bird is one of the largest birds in the world.

clue.text: Oiled lock on temple

parts.note: the temple here is the side of the forehead, and the lock is a small curl of hair pressed flat there, often with oil, rather than a lock on a place of worship

explanation.surface: A greased padlock on the door of a shrine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'temple' and 'lock' suggest a door to a sacred building; the temple is the side of the head and the lock a curl of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: This small flat curl of hair, fixed against the forehead or cheek, was a fashionable style.

clue.text: Angel-punter?

explanation.surface: Two words joined, suggesting a heavenly being who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: An angel is a financial supporter of a show, and a punter is a gambler who stakes money on a horse; both put money behind something.

clue.text: Change station, register complaint

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A commuter changes trains at a station and files a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' rearranges all the letters of STATION and REGISTER; 'complaint' is in its medical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammation of the stomach and intestines is a medical complaint, an ailment rather than a grievance.

clue.text: Most of pudding in sink

indicators.note: most of means dropping the last letter of the word for the pudding

parts.note: sago is a starchy grain made into a milk pudding

explanation.surface: Most of a pudding is left in the kitchen sink.
explanation.walkthrough: SAGO loses its final O.
explanation.definitionFit: To droop or subside downwards is to sink.

clue.text: Respects judges

explanation.surface: A short phrase about honouring the bench.
explanation.definitionFit: Respects as in 'give my respects' are good wishes, and to judge is to consider or look upon something in a certain way.

clue.text: Empty warning of schoolboys coming up to university-tea, possibly?

indicators.note: in a down answer coming up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: cave, Latin for 'beware', was the British public-school pupil's warning that a teacher was coming

indicators.note: possibly signals that tea is one arrangement of its letters, so they are reordered

explanation.surface: Schoolboys shout a warning and empty the room before a university tea party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns CAVE to EVAC; 'possibly' rearranges TEA to ATE. CAVE (said KAY-vee) was British schoolboy slang for 'look out'.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear people out of a building, or to void, is to empty it.

clue.text: Ailing dainty boy a bit short of inner defensive substance

indicators.note: ailing means unwell, out of sorts, so the letters are rearranged
a bit short means one letter is dropped from the words, here a Y

explanation.surface: A sickly, delicate boy is a little lacking in physical defences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit short' drops one Y from DAINTY BOY, and 'Ailing' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A protein made by the immune system to neutralise invaders is the body's internal defence.

clue.text: Celebrity taken in by substandard counterfeit

indicators.note: taken in by means the celebrity word goes inside the word for substandard

parts.note: bad means of poor quality, substandard
a star is a famous person, a celebrity

explanation.surface: A famous person is fooled by a poor-quality fake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in by' puts STAR inside BAD.
explanation.definitionFit: In an old sense the word means spurious or not genuine, as with a fake.

clue.text: A divine annexe talked about?

parts.note: a divine is a theologian, who may hold the degree DD, Doctor of Divinity

explanation.surface: A clergyman's extension to the house becomes the talk of the parish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'talked about?' hints that A + DD read out sounds like the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To annex is to attach or append, so to annexe something is to add it.

clue.text: Needle injury?

parts.note: not a wound from a sharp point, but the hurt caused when someone needles or provokes you

explanation.surface: A medical query about a jab from a syringe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needle' looks like a sharp instrument; it is the verb meaning to annoy, and the hurt feelings that result are the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being needled causes hurt feelings or resentment, which is what one takes.

clue.text: Standing by for green-light spot in a play

parts.note: standing by means waiting
taken as written
a green light means go
a dot is a small spot

explanation.surface: A driver waits at the lights for the signal to move on.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Beckett's 1953 drama, in which two tramps wait for someone who never arrives, is a celebrated play.

clue.text: Bloomer of mixed choir taking wrong tuning-note?

indicators.note: a mixed choir also suggests the letters of choir are mixed up

parts.note: the orchestra tunes to A, so a wrong tuning note is another note, here D

explanation.surface: A mixed choir sings off-key after being given the wrong note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges CHOIR to ORCHI; orchestras tune to A, so the 'wrong' note is D. 'Bloomer' is a flower, not a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: This exotic flowering plant is something that blooms.

clue.text: Old prayer of Orsino in trouble

indicators.note: in trouble suggests disorder, so the letters of the name are rearranged

explanation.surface: Orsino, the lovesick duke of Twelfth Night, prays when in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' rearranges ORSINO, a character in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic word is a prayer, used in Shakespeare.

clue.text: Rare trout with head of bream is a flatfish!

indicators.note: rare suggests something unusual, so the letters are rearranged
head of means the first letter of bream

explanation.surface: An angler exclaims over a rare catch among the fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rare' rearranges TROUT with B, from 'head of bream'.
explanation.definitionFit: This large European fish lies flat on the seabed, a flatfish like a halibut.

clue.text: Choosing the best of city taking on Celtic, perhaps

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London

indicators.note: perhaps hints that Celtic is only one ordering of these letters

explanation.surface: A city team signs Celtic's best players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges CELTIC to LECTIC; Celtic is a Glasgow football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Selecting from many sources rather than following one is a broad-ranging, selective approach.

clue.text: One advanced a bit that is charged

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
on means forward, advanced

explanation.surface: A soldier advanced a short way and was charged.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom or molecule carrying an electrical charge is a charged particle.

clue.text: Atelier mostly bookish?

indicators.note: mostly means the word is cut short at its end

parts.note: studious means fond of study, bookish

explanation.surface: An artist's workshop for a mostly scholarly person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts US from the end of STUDIOUS. Atelier is French for an artist's workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's workroom is a workshop or atelier.

clue.text: Standing advanced in Devon

parts.note: credit is reputation or standing
on means forward, advanced

explanation.surface: Someone's reputation improved down in the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: The town is a market town in Devon, a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: This market town lies in the English county of Devon, so it is a place found there.
